Basic Site Information (unchanged from last submission)

The HWRT Terminal - Norris City, LLC (HWRT) facility, located at 317, County Road 750 North, Norris City, Illinois, is a terminal for the storage and distribution of various fuels.  Petroleum products (i.e., gasoline and diesel) are received by pipeline.  Transport trucks deliver ethanol, biodiesel, and other additives to the facility.  Transport trucks deliver the products to the facility's customers.  

HWRT qualifies as a Program Level 3 for Butane Injection under NAICS 42471 - Petroleum Bulk Stations.  The butane injection  process includes a 30,000-gallon butane storage tank. Butane has been identified by the Environmental Protection Agency as a regulated substance subject to 40 CFR Part 68, which required the preparation of this Risk Management Plan (RMP).  HWRT is also subject to the OSHA process safety management standard and is submitting a program level 3 Risk Management Plan. No other RPM Program chemical substances are in use at or above threshold quantities at this facility. 

The initial construction of the terminal facility was completed in 1960, and it included construction of Tanks NC-01 through NC-04 for petroleum product st

orage.  HWRT Terminal - Norris City, LLC purchased the terminal from Crown Central Petroleum Corporation in 2004.

The facility is located on Cherry Street, approximately 0.5 mile west of U.S. Highway 1 and 0.25 mile north of Main Street in Norris City.  The immediate vicinity is sparsely populated; however, the closest residence is across the street from the facility's exit gate.  The facility has fuel and additive storage tanks with capacities ranging from 300 to 2,524,116 gallons.  Each of these fuel tanks is provided with adequate secondary containment.  

The butane injection process is fairly simple.  Liquefied butane gas is delivered in tank trucks and pumped into the butane tank.  Butane is stored under pressure at ambient temperatures.  Butane is injected into gasoline by pumping it into the pipeline as the gasoline is being delivered to an HWRT storage tank.  The butane injection into gasoline delivery pipeline can occur either from the butane storage tank or directly from the tank truck unloading butane.

HWRT's Compliance Policy (unchanged from last submission)

It is HWRT's policy to adhere to all applicable federal, state and local rules and regulations. The owners and management of this facility regard employee and public safety as a very serious matter and have taken many precautions to maintain a safe working and public environment.  Some of these precautions include:

Preparing and implementing a Facility Response Plan (FRP);
Complying with NFPA 58 Liquefied Petroleum Gas Code
Annual inspections of the butane system by a qualified outside contractor;
Preparing and implementing a Spill, Prevention, Control and Countermeasure (SPCC) Plan;
Instituting safe operating procedures;
Training employees in safety programs and procedures; and
Coordinating with the Local Emergency Planning Committee (LEPC).

Accident Prevention (unchanged from last submission)

Employees are trained to recognize the hazards of the process and all changes to the process are rev

iewed to ensure that the safety, health, and environmental consequences of the change are addressed prior to making the change. Routine daily, monthly, and annual inspection are conducted to ensure compliance with existing safety policies. The facility has a strong commitment to the safe handling of butane and other flammable materials and to minimize the probability of an accidental release.  This is achieved through a combination of safety equipment, personnel training and operating procedures.  The safety equipment includes excess flow valves, pressure relief valves and emergency shut off valves.  Annual inspections of the Butane system are performed by an experienced, knowledgeable, outside contractor. The condition of the tank, piping, and supports, checking the internal valves, pressure relief valves, emergency shut-off valves and cables, pressure gauge, and liquid pump are key features of the annual inspection. 

Five-year Accident History  (unchanged from last submission)

This facility has not had a release of butane or other regulated substance as defined in 40 CFR 68.3 and 68.130 or any OSHA highly hazardous chemical as defined in 40 CFR 29.1910(b) in the last 5 years.

Emergency Response Program (unchanged from last submission)

The facility emergency response programs include FRP and SPCC Plans.  The FRP includes information regarding emergency response, hazard identification, various discharge scenarios, descriptions of periodic drills and exercises and describes employee training.  The SPCC Plan includes similar information as well as facility inspection forms.  Employees are typically provided with emergency response training, on-the-job training, spill prevention and spill response training and other supplemental training.

The Facility Response Plan contains specific actions to be taken in response to an accidental release of butane, procedures to inform the public about a release, and first aid and toxicity information regarding butane.  All emplo

yees working with butane are trained in handling flammable materials and are provided with annual refresher training.  A copy of this plan has been sent to the White County LEPC.  The telephone number for the LEPC is 618-384-4701.
